expectation: Membrane or cytoplasmic signal on small round cells with lobed nuclei (neutrophils, some eosinophils). Usually scattered single cells in the mucosal stroma or near vessels, sparse unless the tissue is inflamed, where they cluster in exudate or crypt abscesses.
observed: A: haze follows the tissue, with bright round blobs on and off it and glow along the top edge and muscle streaks. B/C: stromal haze, one blob, few faint dots. D: ring-like cells, but at the glowing edge. E: CD11b is only haze.
why: Signal follows tissue outline, edges and debris. The only cell-like cluster sits in the edge glow, and no scattered specific population shows at tissue scale.
notes: CD66b looks like haze that follows the tissue, plus off-tissue blobs and edge or fibre glow. The ring-shaped cells in D sit on the glowing top edge, so they are not convincing. CD11b has no cellular structure, so row E cannot help.
